data.summary: This 16‑week plan starts with the student’s weak units (Atomic Structure and Compound Structure) and interleaves new material with review. Each week is a single 4‑hour block of focused study, including a concrete task and, when available, a live class that matches the week’s topics. The last two weeks are dedicated to mixed review and timed practice to solidify knowledge before the exam.

tasks: Read the textbook section on moles and molar mass, then solve 10 practice problems on converting grams to moles and vice versa.
Watch a recorded lecture on mass spectroscopy, then annotate the key peaks for three elements. Create a summary sheet of how mass spectra reveal isotopic composition.
Do 15 problems calculating elemental composition of pure substances and mixtures. Mark each answer against the scoring guide.
Create a chart of periodic trends (atomic radius, ionization energy, electronegativity). Use it to predict valence electrons and ionic compound formation for five elements.
Attend live class 9300. After class, review the lecture notes and solve 10 problems on bond types and potential energy curves.
Read the chapter on ionic solids and metals. Then, write a short paragraph comparing lattice energy and metallic bonding, citing at least two examples.
Practice drawing Lewis diagrams for 12 molecules, including resonance cases. Check each diagram against the formal charge rules.
Attend live class 9301. Post‑class, solve 8 resonance structure problems and 5 VSEPR geometry questions, then self‑grade using the rubric.
Do a concept map linking types of intermolecular forces to physical properties of solids. Then, answer 10 multiple‑choice questions on the topic.
Solve 12 ideal gas law problems, including partial pressure and combined gas law scenarios. Follow up with 5 kinetic molecular theory questions.
Create a reaction worksheet: write net ionic equations for 8 reactions, then balance each full equation. Verify each step with a stoichiometry calculation.
Conduct a virtual lab simulation on reaction rates. Record data, plot rate vs. concentration, and write a brief report interpreting the rate law.
Solve 10 calorimetry problems, then draw and label energy diagrams for two exothermic and two endothermic reactions.
Calculate equilibrium constants for 5 reactions. Then, predict the direction of shift when concentration or pressure changes.
Compute pH for 6 solutions (strong and weak). Create a buffer capacity table for two buffer systems and explain the effect of adding a strong acid.
Take a 60‑minute timed practice quiz covering all reviewed topics. Afterward, review mistakes and update a personal error log.

data.final_week_advice: In the final week, focus on consolidating knowledge through timed practice and error analysis. Use the review log to target lingering weak spots before the exam.
